Liberty Energy.why: Liberty Power Innovations builds and operates on-site natural-gas generation for hyperscale / AI data-center campuses (3 GW secured through 2029), so AI data-center power demand drives its power revenue
Liberty Energy.evidence: Liberty Energy Q2 FY2026 (07-23-2026): CEO - JV with PowerBridge for the 2 GW Alpha Digital Campus (over 300 MW initial generation, first power Q4 2027) for 'hyperscale, AI, and other large load customers'; equipment agreements with Bergen Engines and Wärtsilä

players.product: On-site natural-gas power generation for AI data centers and large loads (Liberty Power Innovations: multi-OEM reciprocating-engine generation stacks with BESS, energy management and ERCOT/PJM market participation)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 revenue was $1.2 billion versus $1 billion in the prior quarter; CFO: the 16% sequential increase reflected record utilization, a modest pricing uplift and higher product sales; adjusted EBITDA $151 million; net income $43 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $1.2 billion; +16% QoQ; adjusted EBITDA $151 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Liberty formed a JV with PowerBridge (a Five Point Infrastructure portfolio company) focused on PowerBridge's Alpha Digital Campus, a planned 2 GW powered campus in West Texas; the initial phase is expected to include over 300 MW of generation capacity, first power anticipated in Q4 2027 with development continuing through 1H 2028; discussions with prospective data center tenants on power offtake are underway. CFO: no leases are booked yet; customer leases will be announced when signed; JV finalization in the near term. Early generation will be behind the meter, with a grid interconnection likely in 2028 (a Batch Zero area).
quarterly_data.figure: 2 GW campus; over 300 MW initial phase; first power Q4 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: during the quarter Liberty secured multiple agreements to purchase power generation equipment with Bergen Engines, Wärtsilä and other global suppliers. CFO: with near-term executions it will have secured the 3 GW planned through the end of 2029, plus late 2029 / early 2030 deliveries. CEO: 'We have line of sight to that inbound 3 GW', and beyond that into late 2029 and early 2030.

CFO: Liberty now anticipates approximately $1.5 billion of capital expenditures in 2026, primarily reflecting increased deposit payments to secure long lead time power generation; Q2 net capex and long-term deposits were $221 million, including $71 million of power generation deposits.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 capex ~$1.5 billion; Q2 power generation deposits $71 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: building the 3 GW will take somewhere between $5 billion and $6 billion of capex, an all-in cost including BESS (an average of 50% BESS for data center clients) and inflation through 2029 deliveries; about a quarter will be spent by the end of this year. CFO: 'generation is an incredibly short supply'; early-year equipment deposits came in a little higher than modeled in January.

CEO: power return target unchanged at a five-six-year cash-on-cash payback and 17%-18% unlevered rate of return; the first part of the 300 MW runs by late 2027, with meaningful income-statement impact from power generation from 2028. CFO: full income-statement fall-through of the 3 GW by the end of 2029; price increases pass through ('We don't see pushback on the pricing').
quarterly_data.figure: 17%-18% unlevered return; 3 GW by end of 2029

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Liberty announced a strategic alliance with SLB combining Liberty's integrated power solutions with SLB's modular infrastructure for power and electrical infrastructure inside and outside the data center, with future collaboration on hybrid power systems, digital energy management, advanced power architectures and waste heat recovery.

CFO: Vantage is a data center builder with which Liberty has a dedicated commercial relationship and will have dedicated power for its facilities; Liberty also works with a number of powered land developers and data center builders. Permits are filed and community engagement is underway for a project with a data center builder in Wyoming.

CEO: Liberty formed Liberty Wholesale Commodities for direct participation in ERCOT power markets and can now integrate on-site generation with both ERCOT and PJM market participation for large load customers. CEO: the commercial pipeline has migrated to a smaller number of larger opportunities, with more gigawatt-plus campuses built in phases from a few hundred megawatts to several gigawatts.

Completions business: record pump hours and horsepower hours in Q2; CEO: Q3 utilization looks quite strong with very modest white space in the calendar, Liberty continues to push for higher service prices into Q3 and maybe Q4, while sand and chemical margins remain challenged; a new digiPrime fleet built for Canada (replacement, not additive) is being delivered over 2H 2026; outlook for 2027 remains quite positive.
